texts: mixed: the exchange, both villages and the Faltern group all come through, but "lantern-keepers" is welded into one kind symbol that is recorded only as a kind of keeper - nothing in the parse says these keepers keep lanterns, so "who keeps lanterns in Faltern?" finds nothing there. Say it in its own clause: "Keepers from Aelmere exchange letters with the keepers of Faltern, who keep lanterns." One caveat that is our fault rather than your wording: "exchange ... with" between a whole class (any Keeper from Aelmere) and one definite group (the Faltern keepers) has no settled shape in our instruction set yet, so that half of the parse may come out differently on a re-parse.
good. the "on this coast" restriction survives as a condition on the rule rather than being dropped, and the denial covers the whole keeping predication.
good. a plain habitual keeping event with Aelmere as the doer and lanterns as a non-specific object, and no kind invented for Aelmere that the sentence does not state.
